The '''non-mass S-thread booster''' was a type of [[S-thread booster/Legends|S-thread booster]] that could be planted in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] used hundreds of non-mass [[Simu-tunnel/Legends|S-thread]] boosters to keep open the unstable [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] known as the [[Byss Run/Legends|Byss Run]], and during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], it also utilized non-mass S-thread boosters to create the secret [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]] route leading to the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]].

==Description==
The non-mass S-thread booster was a type of [[S-thread booster/Legends|S-thread booster]], a device that could be used to brute-force open a new [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] tunnel and then keep the newly created [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] open. Non-mass [[Simu-tunnel/Legends|S-thread]] boosters could be planted in hyperspace.<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
[[File:ByssRun-TEA.png|thumb|right|300px|The Galactic Empire used non-mass S-thread boosters to keep open the unstable Byss Run hyperlane.]]
At one point, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] began using, at staggering expense, hundreds of<ref name="TEA" /> advanced<ref name="FDCR">[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Force and Destiny'' Core Rulebook]]</ref> non-mass S-thread boosters to maintain a winding, perilous,<ref name="TEA" /> and fragile<ref name="FDCR" /> secret [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] military hyperspace route&mdash;eventually known as the [[Byss Run/Legends|Byss Run]]&mdash;that had been [[Star map/Legends|mapped]] during the tenure of Republic [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]<ref name="TEA" /> between [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] and [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]]<ref name="PalpatineDates">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' establishes that the [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] that corresponded with the eventual [[Byss Run/Legends|Byss Run]] was [[Star map/Legends|charted]] during [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] first [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] as [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]], which corresponds to between [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] and [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] per ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> and that connected the [[Empress Teta system/Legends|Empress Teta system]] to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] Palpatine's personal retreat [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] in the [[Beshqek system]].<ref name="TEA" />

During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Empire also began the construction of the [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] over the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor]], in the [[Endor system/Legends|Endor system]]<ref name="Endor">{{GamerCite|9|Endor and the Moddell Sector}}</ref> of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Moddell sector/Legends|Moddell sector]].<ref name="TEA" /> To allow for expeditious&mdash;and secret&mdash;transportation of the necessary materials and components to Endor, the Empire used non-mass S-thread boosters to extend the [[Silvestri Trace]] hyperlane from<ref name="Endor" /> the planet<ref name="TEA" /> [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]]<ref name="Endor" /> of the Outer Rim's [[Brema sector/Legends|Brema sector]]<ref name="EAOC Sullust">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]]</ref> directly to Endor,<ref name="Endor" /> with the Moddell [[Sector/Legends|sector's]] [[Murk system/Legends|Murk system]] becoming a penultimate stop on the new hyperspace route, known as the [[Sanctuary Pipeline/Legends|Sanctuary Pipeline]].<ref name="TEA" /> Following the Imperial defeat by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Endor" /> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] and criminal allies of the Alliance stole any S-thread boosters of the Sanctuary Pipeline that they could find, and the route eventually became largely [[Navigator/Legends|unnavigable]].<ref name="Endor" />

==Behind the scenes==
The non-mass S-thread booster was first mentioned in the article "[[Endor and the Moddell Sector]]," which was authored by [[Craig Robert Carey]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Jason Fry]] and was published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 9|ninth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine<ref name="Endor" /> on [[February 22]], [[2002]].<ref name="GamerDate">{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20020222.html|text=Starfighters Soar in Gamer #9}}</ref>
